title: Behavior-Based Safety
overview: This course is designed to provide managers and safety professionals with an in-depth understanding of their role in implementing and assessing the effectiveness of safety programs. "How to be a Leader in Safety and Health" emphasizes the importance of top management’s involvement in guiding the implementation of new health and safety initiatives. It explores the change management process, which can often present challenges for organizations aiming to improve their safety performance. When traditional risk reduction methods fail to achieve the desired outcomes, a new strategy must be introduced. Through real-life examples and interactive exercises, participants will be guided through a step-by-step process that enables them to influence safety policies and procedures within their organizations. Additionally, participants will be equipped to take on leadership roles in promoting and implementing effective health and safety practices.
audience: This course is aimed at safety officers and other safety professionals involved in the development and implementation of safety practices, as well as those working to integrate safety into the broader organizational culture.
methodology: This course is highly interactive and participatory, incorporating a variety of pedagogical methods to ensure participants can operate effectively in multi-functional environments. It is built on four key learning pillars: concept learning (lectures and presentations), role playing (group exercises), experience sharing (roundtable discussions), and exposure to real-world challenges and policy decisions.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand the roles of management, employees, and communication in improving organizational safety and health.
Design hazard analysis and control strategies, along with Emergency Action Plans (EAP).
Develop skills in safety supervision, leadership, and evaluation.
Establish and lead a safety culture program.
Evaluate and assess the effectiveness of safety and health culture programs post-implementation
